title: PolynomialDualityRestrictionAtlas
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism and $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-scheme] and [def-pc-derived-category], and use the polynomial charts and their coinduced models [def-trf-polynomial-duality-presentation-data]. Write $A_C=(P_C,i_{C*}\mathcal O_{U_C})$, $g_C:U_C\to A_C$, and $h_C:A_C\to P_C$ for the direct-image algebra space and its canonical maps [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. Use actual unbounded derived direct images [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] and their original-unit-normalized composition [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition]. A polynomial restriction atlas for $K$ consists of exactness proof data for the scalar-forgetting functors, and isomorphisms $Rg_{C*}(K|_{U_C})\cong H_C(\Omega^{n_C}_{P_C/S}[n_C])$ for every chart, where $H_C$ is the derived coinduction of its evaluation adjunction [lem-sc-sheaf-coinduction-adjunction]. Require the following canonical restriction equation. For source and ambient open immersions $r:U_D\to U_C$ and $a:P_D\to P_C$, an algebra-space map $b:A_D\to A_C$ satisfying $h_Da=bh_C$ and $g_Db=rg_C$, equal dimensions and equal structural maps to $S$, let $F\dashv Rb_*$ be any left adjoint. Restrict the top forms by the isomorphism sending every local wedge to the wedge under canonical differential restriction [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. When the exchange mate from $a^*T_C$ to $T_DF$, formed from the unit of $F\dashv Rb_*$ and the actual direct-image square, is invertible on the coinduced coefficient, define model restriction as the coinduction adjunct of its inverse followed by restriction of evaluation. Define source restriction by the mate of the actual open-restriction unit on $K$, followed by the native exact restriction-composition isomorphism. The atlas equation is $F(\alpha_C)$ followed by model restriction equals source restriction followed by $\alpha_D$. These are specified canonical arrows, independently of the atlas identifications; their identity and composition conventions are the native restriction and original-unit composition conventions. The shared canonical primitives are those of [def-trf-polynomial-duality-restriction-primitives].
